subject: Snapshot testing and reviewed baseline comparison

evals.prompt: Define snapshot testing in 2-3 sentences. Include capture, stored baseline, comparison, diff review, and update approval.
expected_elements: Captures output from a known-good run
Stores the output as a baseline snapshot or golden file
Compares future output against that baseline
Treats a mismatch as a diff requiring human review
Updates the baseline only after confirming the change is intentional

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of snapshot testing. Name at least seven primitives and show how they relate.
expected_elements: At least seven of: target output, snapshot artifact, serializer, baseline, comparison algorithm, diff, approval cycle, update command, deterministic input control, reviewer, version control
Explains the snapshot artifact is the assertion
Explains the diff is the decision surface
Explains approval changes the baseline and rejection means fixing production or test code
Explains deterministic output is a precondition for low-churn snapshots

evals.prompt: Why does snapshot testing exist? Name the output types and failure modes it is meant to handle.
expected_elements: Useful when complex output would be expensive to hand-specify
Names data, DOM/HTML, text/file/generated output, or visual/image snapshots
Surfaces structural or visual drift for review
Supports characterization of legacy behavior before refactoring
Prevents unnoticed output changes when reviewers actually inspect diffs
Does not replace explicit behavioral assertions

evals.prompt: Distinguish snapshot testing from testing strategy, property-based testing, test-driven development, test doubles, e2e test design, and diff analysis.
expected_elements: testing-strategy chooses the overall mix, levels, and cadence
property-based-testing asserts universal properties over generated inputs
test-driven-development owns strict test-first workflow
test-doubles-design owns fake/stub/mock collaborators
e2e-test-design owns user-journey correctness across a running system
diff-analysis helps inspect changes but does not define snapshot baseline policy
snapshot-testing owns capture-and-compare baseline artifacts and approval discipline

evals.prompt: Classify data snapshots, DOM snapshots, text/file snapshots, and visual snapshots. What makes each stable or unstable?
expected_elements: Data snapshots serialize objects or API responses
DOM snapshots serialize markup or component trees
Text/file snapshots compare generated files, CLI output, SQL, or logs
Visual snapshots compare screenshots with pixel/perceptual thresholds
Stability requires controlling timestamps, random IDs, order, locale, environment, and rendering variance
Visual snapshots require stable browser/platform/font/rendering environment or service

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A component snapshot changes in every PR because IDs, current time, and object key order appear in the snapshot. Developers now run update-snapshot automatically. Diagnose and repair the testing practice.
expected_elements: Identifies snapshot churn from nondeterministic output
Rejects automatic baseline update without review
Controls time, IDs, key/order, locale, or serializers
Keeps snapshots small/readable or replaces with targeted assertions
Requires reviewers to inspect diffs before accepting baseline changes

evals.prompt: Correct this statement: 'Snapshot tests are automatic regression tests, so if they fail we can just run the update command and commit the new snapshot.'
expected_elements: Rejects update-without-review as removing test value
Requires reading the diff
Distinguishes intentional changes from bugs
Updates baseline only for intentional changes
Fixes production or test code when the diff is unintentional
Mentions snapshots should be committed and reviewed like other test assertions

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for snapshot testing that preserves baseline capture, comparison, diff review, and deliberate approval. Then name one bad analogy.
expected_elements: Uses photograph, blueprint, ledger, saved proof, or equivalent baseline analogy
Maps baseline capture to a stored artifact
Maps comparison to noticing differences from the saved artifact
Maps approval to deciding whether the difference is intended
Rejects a bad analogy that treats updating the record without looking as verification
